envelope.description: Wire the authoritative reconcile into daemon boot, preserving first-boot behaviour exactly

body.title: Wire the authoritative reconcile into daemon boot, preserving first-boot behaviour exactly
body.summary: Replace step '2b. Ensure config.json exists with agent defaults' at src/daemon/index.ts:178-203 with an unconditional read → reconcile → write-if-changed via the t7 wrapper. The `if (!existsSync(PATHS.config))` short-circuit goes away: the absent-file case must reduce EXACTLY to today's write-defaults behaviour — not merely a superset — while the previously no-op else branch at L194-203 gains the real reconcile. The hand-rolled L180-192 literal (~17 of 41 catalog rows) is deleted in favour of catalog defaults, so before deleting it, assert key-by-key against the t2 captured literal fixture that each key's catalog default is deep-equal to the literal's value. Any divergence must be surfaced as a deliberate, named default change (key, old value, new value) with its own acceptance check — never absorbed silently, because the unconditional reconcile would also write that divergent value into existing configs that lack the key. Tighten the existing `catch { /* ignore parse errors */ }` at L202 into the explicit no-write-and-warn behaviour. The whole sequence is wrapped so a reconcile failure never aborts boot — copy the non-fatal shape of the legacy-storage sweep immediately above at L154-171 (`warn ... non-fatal, retry on next boot`) — but a ConfigCatalogError is logged distinguishably (an explicit shipped-catalog-bug warn naming the catalog path) so a programmer error in our own catalog does not read as a transient EACCES. No DB dependency: 2b runs before the DB opens at L213. Ship boot integration tests asserting the reconcile is unconditional and that a throwing reconcile still reaches listening state.
acceptanceChecks: src/daemon/index.ts no longer short-circuits on an existing config.json; the reconcile runs on every boot

A test enumerates every key of the deleted L180-192 literal from the t2 captured fixture and asserts the corresponding catalog default is deep-equal to the literal's value; any intended divergence is named in a dedicated check listing the key and its old and new value
With no config.json present, boot writes a document whose values for the former literal's keys are identical to the pre-change output, plus the remaining catalog defaults, in one write
A reconcile that throws or fails (catalog error, unreadable config, write failure) logs exactly one warn line, leaves the on-disk file untouched, and the daemon still reaches listening state
A ConfigCatalogError produces a warn line that names the offending catalog path and is textually distinguishable from a user-config or I/O failure warn
The former silent `catch { /* ignore parse errors */ }` now emits an explicit warn naming the file and the parse failure, and writes nothing
src/daemon imports the catalog from src/config, and grep confirms src/daemon still has zero imports of src/cli

tests.name: daemon boot — reconcile runs on startup unconditionally and does not short-circuit on an existing config.json
daemon boot — a throwing/failing reconcile (catalog error, unreadable config, write failure) logs exactly one warn, leaves the file untouched, and the daemon still reaches listening state
daemon boot — a ConfigCatalogError warn names the offending catalog path and is textually distinguishable from a user-config or I/O warn
daemon boot first-boot equivalence — no config.json present writes the former literal's key values identically to the pre-change output plus the remaining catalog defaults, in one write
daemon boot — the former silent parse-error catch now emits an explicit warn naming the file and the parse failure and writes nothing
defaults-literal parity — every key of the deleted src/daemon/index.ts:180-192 literal (from the t2 fixture) is deep-equal to its catalog default, with any intended divergence named key/old/new
module boundary — src/daemon imports the catalog from src/config and a source scan confirms src/daemon has zero imports of src/cli
